config._note: humaniq-hours-process-redesign (design.md Decision 8, ADR-037 per-change fragment): the HR booking index over TimeEntry. A concrete page rather than an indexScaffold instance because the create-form allowlist keys (includeFields) are not template params. Add is enabled via actionToggles.showAdd — NEVER the dead allowCreate key. The includeFields allowlist is the self-service set PLUS employeeId: HR may book on behalf of an employee, so the picker is the one extra field; userId/administrationId/costCenter/hours stay server-stamped/derived (TimeEntryStampListener) and the process fields live on the parent Timesheet, never here.

config._note: humaniq-hours-process-redesign (design.md Decision 8): one individual booking — detail template B shape (two-panel data + related), authored concrete because the editable-field allowlist needs per-key overrides beyond the simpleDetailScaffold params. NO lifecycleActions: a TimeEntry has no lifecycle of its own — the process lives on the parent Timesheet, and entry mutability is enforced server-side from the parent's state (REQ-TEC-005). The data widget shows the booking fields plus the derived/stamped hours, costCenter and userId display-only (server custody — hours from start/end/break, costCenter from the org chain, userId from the employee link); the editable set is the HR booking allowlist minus employeeId/timesheetId, which the Related panel resolves as links instead (the house FK pattern — reassigning a booking to another employee or timesheet is not a designed journey). origin/administrationId/allocation extension fields stay off the page body (server-stamped bookkeeping; visible via the metadata sidebar where applicable). Audit history is a sidebar tab.

params.note: humaniq-hours-process-redesign (design.md Decision 8): the employee's read-only list of their own period aggregates, per the MijnLoonstroken precedent (REQ-MHS-004) — timesheets are server-created by the booking flow (find-or-create on the entry's startedAt month), and submission happens through the lifecycle actions on TimesheetDetail. Fail-closed @me filter: rows whose employee has no linked account keep userId null and never appear here (REQ-MHS-002).
